lastCompletedGameRecap.recapHeadline: Giants intercept Trevor Lawrence twice and hold on to beat the Jaguars 23-18
lastCompletedGameRecap.recapLeadExcerpt: J.  J.  McCarthy and the New York Giants sputtered for much of the fourth quarter, Jaguars coach Liam Coen decided to kick a late field goal because he was confident Jacksonville would get the ball back with a chance to win.  “As an offense, we took that personal, for sure,” McCarthy said.
lastCompletedGameRecap.inGameInjuryNotes: Injuries Jaguars: Cornerback Jarrian Jones left in the first quarter with a chest injury. ... Left tackle Walker Little left with a knee injury, leading to Wyatt Milum entering. Little was already playing in place of Anton Harrison , who's out for the season. ... Running back Bhayshul Tuten limped off late. Giants: Cornerback Greg Newsome injured an ankle on the first defensive series and did not return. ... Linebacker Kayvon Thibodeaux got medical attention and departed briefly but returned.
lastCompletedGameRecap.upNextNotes: Up next Jaguars: Host the Tennessee Titans next Sunday. Giants: Visit the Indianapolis Colts next Sunday.

injuryReport.name: Cor'Dale Flott
injuryReport.beatComment: Flott exited the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Jaguars early with a neck injury and did not return to the contest. The cornerback remains sidelined due to the recent injury, and it remains unclear how much time he is expected to miss. Flott will need to upgrade his practice participation by Friday to have any shot at playing in Sunday's divisional contest with the Jaguars.

injuryReport.name: Dan Moore Jr.
injuryReport.beatComment: Moore may have picked up the injury during the third quarter, and he's being evaluated by medical staff to determine whether he can return. James Hudson figures to take over at left tackle in Moore's absence.

injuryReport.name: John Franklin-Myers
factors: Wednesday Limited Participation (LP); player toughness prior = 78%
injuryReport.beatComment: Franklin-Meyers played 42 percent of the Titans' snaps in the Week 11 loss to the Cowboys, close to his regular snap share, while playing through a back injury. The defensive tackle will likely continue to practice through the issue in a limited capacity before suiting up for Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

injuryReport.name: Tony Adams
injuryReport.beatComment: Adams has recovered from the illness that sidelined him for the Titans' Week 11 loss to the Cowboys. The safety has already returned to full practice participation and should be all set to continue stringing together prep sessions in anticipation of Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

injuryReport.name: Kylen Granson
injuryReport.beatComment: Granson displayed some pass-catching ability in his first five seasons in the league between stops with the Colts and Eagles, but the Titans have deployed him almost exclusively on special teams in 2026. He's been active for just four of the team's first 10 contests and has drawn just one target while playing three total snaps on offense.

injuryReport.name: Kevin Winston Jr.
injuryReport.beatComment: Winston was able to register at least seven stops for the sixth time this season while playing every defensive snap in Week 11. The safety has now compiled 63 total tackles (35 solo), a forced fumble and a fumble recovery over eight contests so far this season.

injuryReport.name: Carnell Tate
injuryReport.beatComment: Tate had a fairly non-descript day overall despite the Titans' 30-point output, but he rewarded fantasy managers with a 59-yard catch-and run touchdown in the third quarter on which he alertly got up and ran down the left sideline after Cowboys defenders failed to touch him while he was down. The rookie fourth overall pick was making his return from a two-game absence due to a shoulder injury, and the score served as Tate's second of his career, both which have come in his last three games. Tate has at least 58 receiving yards in five of the last six contests, including in three straight, heading into a Week 12 road matchup against the Jaguars next Sunday.

coachingMatchup.headline: Liam Coen & DC Anthony Campanile vs. HC Robert Saleh, OC Brian Daboll & DC Gus Bradley (EverBank Stadium)
coachingMatchup.summary: Week 12 two-sided coordinator chess match pitting Jacksonville Jaguars's staff (Liam Coen, OC Grant Udinski, DC Anthony Campanile) against Tennessee Titans (1-9)—testing both Jacksonville's offensive efficiency and its defensive pass-rush and coverage discipline.
bullets: Pass-Game Efficiency & Coverage Shell Delta: Liam Coen and OC Grant Udinski pair condensed splits with pre-snap jet motion and orbit motion to stress Tennessee Titans's single-high vs. two-high rotations—widening curl/flat defenders to attack the honey-hole between hook/curl linebackers and deep safeties on play-action choice/dagger concepts.

Trench Run-Fit & Two-Way Leverage: Against Tennessee Titans's pin-and-pull, counter, and duo runs targeting the A- and B-gaps, DC Anthony Campanile balances four-man pressure with disguised Quarters and Cover 6 split-safety rotations on early downs and in the red zone.

Money-Down & Red-Zone Execution: Third-down conversion discipline and red-zone touchdown rate govern whether Jacksonville sustains multi-play scoring drives or yields momentum to Tennessee Titans's pass rush and coverage disguises.
Tempo, Turnovers & Venue Leverage: EverBank Stadium situational play-calling, penalty margin, and turnover differential provide the clearest late-game swing factors for both coaching staffs.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Trevor Lawrence, Brenton Strange & Jakobi Meyers vs. CB Joshua Williams & LB Cedric Gray
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: JAX: #9 Pass Off (244.7 yds) · #7 Off. Scoring (+7.31) | TEN: #32 Pass Def (+7.94)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Trevor Lawrence, Brenton Strange & Jakobi Meyers attack the intermediate seams and middle-of-the-field leverage windows against Tennessee Titans's #32 pass defense (+7.94). Winning early-down timing throws keeps Jacksonville's offense ahead of the chains and punishes disguised single-high rotations.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Trevor Lawrence (#16) scanning Titans's deep safeties at the snap—when LB Cedric Gray widens to take away the crossers, the intermediate seam opens immediately for Brenton Strange (#85).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Travon Walker, Josh Hines-Allen & Arik Armstead vs. QB Cam Ward & G Chandler Zavala
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: JAX: #16 Def Sacks (2.3/gm) | TEN: #16 Pass Protection (6.5%)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Travon Walker, Josh Hines-Allen & Arik Armstead lead Jacksonville's #16 NFL pass rush (2.3/gm) against Tennessee Titans's #16 pass-protection unit (6.5%). Collapsing the interior pocket without sending extra blitzers lets Jaguars keep seven defenders in coverage.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: On 3rd-and-6+, watch whether Travon Walker (#44) draw chip help from Titans's tight ends or backs—creating 1-on-1 rush lanes inside for Josh Hines-Allen (#41).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Jessie Bates III, Foyesade Oluokun & Antonio Johnson vs. WR Carnell Tate & QB Cam Ward
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: JAX: #3 Pass Def (-3.58) | TEN: #26 Pass Off (182.6 yds)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Jessie Bates III, Foyesade Oluokun & Antonio Johnson anchor Jacksonville's #3 pass defense (-3.58) against WR Carnell Tate and Tennessee Titans's #26 passing attack (182.6 yds). Limiting explosive 20+ yard chunk plays forces Titans into sustained red-zone drives.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Track Jessie Bates III (#0) at the top of routes against WR Carnell Tate: press-bail alignment with safety help over the top takes away QB Cam Ward's preferred isolation shots.

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Bhayshul Tuten & Parker Washington vs. Titans Front Seven & LB Cedric Gray
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: JAX: #14 Rush Off (113.7 yds) | TEN: #19 Rush Def (-0.35)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Bhayshul Tuten & Parker Washington test Tennessee Titans's #19 run defense (-0.35) with horizontal stretch and interior cutback lanes. Generating 4.5+ yards on first down unlocks play-action explosives and neutralizes Titans's pass-rush packages.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch whether Titans's linebackers over-pursue motion to the perimeter—opening decisive backside B-gap cutback lanes for Bhayshul Tuten (#33).

keyMatchupsMatrix.unitMatchup: Emmanuel Pregnon, Cole Van Lanen & Ezra Cleveland vs. DE Jacob Martin & Titans Simulated Pressures
keyMatchupsMatrix.statComparison: JAX: #16 Pass Protection (6.0%) | TEN: #16 Def Sacks (2.4/gm)
keyMatchupsMatrix.tacticalDetail: Emmanuel Pregnon, Cole Van Lanen & Ezra Cleveland protect Trevor Lawrence (#16 protection at 6.0%) against DE Jacob Martin and Tennessee Titans's #16 pass rush (2.4/gm). Passing off interior twists and simulated blitzes cleanly determines late-down conversion efficiency.
keyMatchupsMatrix.filmTell: Watch Emmanuel Pregnon (#75) on obvious passing downs—if DE Jacob Martin cannot win clean around the arc, Titans must dial up interior stunts that stress Cole Van Lanen (#70).
